title: Autodesk Fusion 360 Pricing 2026: What It Costs a Month
summary: Fusion 360 pricing starts at $680 annually for the core subscription, about $57 per month. See what each plan includes to choose the best fit for you.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and billing limits


Where the quote and the invoice diverge is in extensions, cloud credits, and how you use the software, because the plan price in Autodesk Fusion 360 covers the base application only. Check each against Autodesk's current terms before you commit, since they change.


### Fusion 360 extensions and cloud credits costs


Extensions are paid add-ons that unlock specific capabilities, such as advanced simulation, generative design, or additional machining strategies. They're priced per user per year, so each seat that needs one pays for it separately.


If only two people on a five-person team run simulations, buy two extension seats, not five. Resellers list these yearly prices, and they differ from reseller to reseller, so compare the extension line as carefully as the base plan.


Cloud credits are the second meter. Certain operations, such as cloud simulation, generative design studies, and some rendering, run on Autodesk's servers and consume credits rather than your own machine's time. The unit being metered is the job, not the month.


If you run a few studies a quarter, you will barely notice. Iterate on generative designs daily, though, and you can run through your allotment and have to buy more, so estimate studies per month before you call the plan flat-rate.


### Fusion 360 personal use eligibility and limits


The free personal tier is for non-commercial work, and it carries a revenue ceiling and a hobby-scope definition.


If you sell parts, take paid client work, or run a business on it, you likely don't qualify, and treating it as free is a compliance risk rather than a saving.


When a workflow depends on a feature that is restricted compared with the paid product, you are pushed to a paid plan even if your use is otherwise eligible.


### Storage, collaboration and lapsed subscriptions


Projects live in Autodesk's cloud, and storage and sharing come with caps that vary by plan. If you hand files to outside contractors, check how many collaborators you can invite and whether they need their own paid seat to edit.


A cheap plan that forces every contractor onto a license isn't cheap.


The last cost arrives when a subscription lapses. When a paid plan ends, you generally lose editing and some export rights, while your data stays in the cloud.


> A cheap plan that forces every contractor onto a license isn't cheap.


Getting back in means paying again, so a gap in renewal can stall a live project.
